title: Unsynchronized Table._update_table and shared JSONStorage._handle cause JSON corruption and lost writes under concurrent threads
blast_radius: Multi-threaded web workers or background tasks sharing a TinyDB instance overwrite each other's inserts, throw JSONDecodeError/ValueError, and corrupt the JSON file on disk (43/50 corrupted DBs in testing).
trigger_likelihood: High in multi-threaded Python apps (e.g., Flask/FastAPI threadpools, ThreadPoolExecutor, background workers) sharing a TinyDB instance.
broken_invariant: Concurrent inserts on a TinyDB instance must preserve all committed documents and never corrupt JSONStorage._handle.
root_cause: Table.insert invokes unsynchronized _get_next_id() and _update_table(), which reads the entire DB via JSONStorage.read(), mutates a local table dict in memory, and writes back via a single shared file handle self._handle without any lock around seek(0)/json.load/write/truncate.

reproducer.observed_failure_output: 50/50 trials violated (100.0%): 4 threads calling db.insert() x5 caused 989 lost documents, 629 exceptions (620x JSONDecodeError, 9x ValueError), and 43 corrupt JSON files on disk.

disprover_notes: Audited storages.py, table.py, and database.py; zero threading.Lock, RLock, or file locking primitives exist anywhere in TinyDB.
minimal_fix: Wrap Storage read/write/close and Table mutation/query operations in reentrant threading.RLock (see ThreadSafeAtomicJSONStorage + ThreadSafeTable in docs/CASE-STUDY.md).
regression_test_strategy: Run 50-trial 4-thread barrier insert test asserting 0% violations, 20/20 persisted docs per trial, and 0 JSONDecodeError exceptions.

title: Compound update-then-insert in Table.upsert suffers TOCTOU duplicate row creation even with thread-safe storage
blast_radius: Fixing JSONStorage locking alone still allows concurrent Table.upsert() calls on identical natural keys to both observe updated_docs=[] and both fall through to insert(), creating up to 4x duplicate rows.
trigger_likelihood: High whenever multiple threads initialize or update keyed records concurrently via upsert().
broken_invariant: Concurrent Table.upsert() calls matching the same query key must produce exactly one logical document without creating duplicates.
root_cause: Table.upsert executes self.update(document, cond, doc_ids) at tinydb/table.py:615 and checks if updated_docs is empty before calling self.insert(document) at line 623 as two separate _update_table() transactions with no table-level mutex spanning both steps.

reproducer.observed_failure_output: 38/50 trials violated (76.0%) against ThreadSafeAtomicJSONStorage: 4 concurrent threads upserting 3 natural keys created 60 duplicate rows (max 4x copies for one key) and 12 duplicate-ID ValueErrors.

disprover_notes: Confirmed storage-level locking serializes each call individually but releases between self.update() and self.insert(), leaving the compound TOCTOU window wide open.
minimal_fix: Protect Table.upsert (alongside insert/update/remove/read) with a per-Table threading.RLock so check-update-or-insert runs atomically.
regression_test_strategy: Run 50-trial 4-thread barrier upsert() benchmark against ThreadSafeAtomicJSONStorage asserting 0 duplicate rows across all keys.

title: In-place seek(0)->write->truncate in JSONStorage.write destroys previously committed DB on mid-write ENOSPC/EIO
blast_radius: Any partial write or ENOSPC error overwrites the live database file prefix at byte 0 before trailing old bytes remain intact, rendering the entire JSON file unparseable and destroying 100% of prior records.
trigger_likelihood: Medium-High on full disks, quota limits, container ephemeral-storage eviction, or process crashes during DB serialization.
broken_invariant: Previously committed DB records on disk must remain valid and intact if JSONStorage.write() encounters a mid-write I/O or ENOSPC failure.
root_cause: JSONStorage.write seeks self._handle back to byte 0 and writes directly over the live database file prior to calling flush/fsync/truncate instead of staging into a sibling temp file and atomically replacing via os.replace().

reproducer.observed_failure_output: 50/50 trials corrupted (100.0%): injecting ENOSPC after 32 bytes destroyed all 20 previously committed documents in every trial (0/50 valid JSON files recovered).

disprover_notes: Verified os.fsync and truncate happen after in-place write(serialized) overwrites the live handle starting at offset 0.
minimal_fix: Write serialized JSON to a sibling temporary file, flush and os.fsync the temp descriptor, close the live handle on Windows if open, and swap atomically via os.replace(tmp_path, path).
regression_test_strategy: Keep mid-write ENOSPC partial-write injection test asserting 100% committed record preservation and 0 stray .tmp files.

title: touch() creates database files without fsyncing parent directory metadata
broken_invariant: Newly created database files and parent directories must survive sudden OS power loss without losing directory entries.
root_cause: touch() in tinydb/storages.py opens a newly created file in 'a' mode and exits without opening and fsyncing the parent directory file descriptor on POSIX filesystems.
unresolved_fact: Whether parent directory entry loss triggers cleanly on ext4/xfs/APFS under abrupt VM power-off without OS block-layer fault injection.
why_blocked: Userland Python fault injection cannot interrupt POSIX directory-entry metadata journaling between open(O_CREAT) and directory flush.
safe_verification_recipe: Run inside an isolated QEMU/dm-flakey Linux VM: create new TinyDB file, simulate sudden power-cut before sync, remount filesystem, and verify file presence.

title: Candidate iterator invalidation (RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration) in Table.remove(cond=...)
disprover_evidence: Table.remove iterates over list(table.keys()) rather than table.items(), snapshotting keys prior to table.pop(doc_id). Executed 50 trials inserting 200 docs and removing 100 matching docs: 0 RuntimeErrors across 50/50 trials.
rejection_reason: Explicit list(table.keys()) key snapshot prevents dictionary mutation during predicate evaluation and removal.
